      • USER_USB_PORT1

        public static final int USER_USB_PORT1
        User USB port1: the first outer USB port that available for end user.

        I-Series 4.0: - The TYPE-A USB port on board - Android download port

        backpack 4.0: - The TYPE-C USB port on board

        See Also:
        Constant Field Values

      • USER_USB_PORT2

        public static final int USER_USB_PORT2
        User USB port2: the second outer USB port that available for end user.

        I-Series 4.0: - The TYPE-C USB port on board - support DP function

        backpack 4.0: - The outer Type A USB port port near LAN port - At the up layer

        Value: Not exit this USB port

        See Also:
        Constant Field Values

      • USER_USB_PORT3

        public static final int USER_USB_PORT3
        User USB port3: the third outer USB port that available for end user.

        I-Series 4.0: - The micro-USB port at the left of the unit - Near TYPE-C USB port - has ID PIN

        backpack 4.0: - The outer Type A USB port port near LAN port - At the down layer

        Value: Not exit this USB port

      • USB_BOOST_MODE_NONE

        public static final int USB_BOOST_MODE_NONE
        Deprecated.
        Deprecated in handheld and i-series 4.0 models, these models donesn't support USB boost, but for ELO sdk backward-compatibility, don't remove it directly.
        USB electrical signaling drive strength Boost Bit for USB Port:

        '00' = Normal electrical drive strength = No boost

        '01' = Elevated electrical drive strength = Low (approximately 4% boost)

        '10' = Elevated electrical drive strength = Medium (approximately 8% boost)

        '11' = Elevated electrical drive strength = High (approximately 12% boost)

        See Also:

    • Method Detail

      • enableUsbPort

        public void enableUsbPort​(int port,
                          boolean enable,
                          @Nullable
                          android.os.Message onComplete)
        Request to enable/disable data role of the given USB port on the main board.

        Note: For ELO sdk backward-compatibility, Don't remove it directly, Use enableUsbPort(int, boolean, int, Message) instead.

        Parameters:
        port - is the port id that you are requesting to enable/disable, define in EloPeripheralManager.UsbPort
        enable - is a boolean representing the state that you are requesting, true for enabled, false for disabled.
        onComplete - a callback message when the action is completed.if onComplete is null, don't send callback message when completed. the operation Boolean result will be put in onComplete.data with Bundle: Bundle b = new Bundle(); b.putBoolean("result", success); onComplete.setData(b);

      • enableUsbPort

        public void enableUsbPort​(int port,
                          boolean enable,
                          int roleFlag,
                          @Nullable
                          android.os.Message onComplete)
        Request to enable/disable data or power role of the given USB port on the main board. Similar to enableUsbPort(int, boolean, Message), but with the given role flag to indicate switch data or power role.
        Specified by:
        enableUsbPort in interface UsbPortSwitcher
        Parameters:
        port - is the port id that you are requesting to enable/disable, define in EloPeripheralManager.UsbPort
        enable - is a boolean representing the state that you are requesting, true for enabled, false for disabled.
        roleFlag - indicate to switch data role, power role, or both, see ROLE_FLAG_XXX in UsbPortSwitcher
        onComplete - a callback message when the action is completed.if onComplete is null, don't send callback message when completed. the operation Boolean result will be put in onComplete.data with Bundle: Bundle b = new Bundle(); b.putBoolean("result", success); onComplete.setData(b);

      • setUsbBoostMode

        @Deprecated
public void setUsbBoostMode​(int boostMode,
                            @Nullable
                            android.os.Message onComplete)
        Deprecated.
        Deprecated in handheld and i-series 4.0 models, these models donesn't support usb boost, but for ELO sdk backward-compatibility, don't remove it directly.
        Set USB boost mode to elevate the USB signaling strength of the powered USB port.

        These models support USB boost setting:

        "Elo-PP-15" (Paypoint 2.0)

        Note: the powered USB port of Paypoint 2.0 is USER_USB_PORT2 as defined above.

        Parameters:
        boostMode - one of USB_BOOST_MODE_XXX as defined above.
        onComplete - a callback message when the action is completed.if onComplete is null, don't send callback message when completed.
